messages:
Hannah Li: Quick onboarding question: I'm setting up CI to run both functional and perf checks. Functional tests should hit sandbox, perf should hit hosted. I want to swap keys mid-run automatically. Any gotchas with key propagation or webhook alerts I should know?
Ethan Cole: Welcome! Mid-run swaps are fine but note long-lived HTTP/2 connections keep the old auth until reconnect. If your CI uses persistent connections, plan to restart the worker or rotate connections.
Hannah Li: How do teams usually automate the swap so it's safe?
Maya Chen: Common pattern: 1) request 2 ephemeral hosted keys from ops, 2) run sandbox functional tests, 3) start perf runner with key A, then at swap time spin up new connections with key B and drain key A. Ops can issue keys with a short overlap window.
Hannah Li: Who do I request ephemeral keys from and what's the ticket format?
Ethan Cole: Ops via ops-team@redwood.ai. Ticket example: "ephemeral keys x2 for Hannah Li, window 2026-04-05 04:00-04:45 UTC, perf runner ~10k reqs, model: redwood-medium, source: GH Actions via shared-CI-NAT, billing owner: hannah.manager@redwood.ai"
Hannah Li: Cool. Any quick CLI to check a key's type and allowed scopes before swapping?
Maya Chen: Use the keys endpoint: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys/me | jq '.key_type, .scopes, .expires_at'`
Hannah Li: Nice. I also want to post alerts to our CI channel if 429s spike during perf. Is there a webhook or metric feed?
Ethan Cole: Console -> Alerts can send webhooks on metrics like 429s or QPS per-key. Create an alert: condition 429 rate > 1% for 1m -> webhook to your CI slack bot. Ops can help seed the alert for ephemeral keys.
Hannah Li: If I see 429s, what's the immediate remediation? Backoff, rotate key, or pause runners?
Maya Chen: Short term: backoff with jitter. If you still see 429s, rotate to the secondary ephemeral key and spread requests. For CI bursts consider lowering concurrency or throttling at the client. Ops can also apply a short qps guard.
Hannah Li: Is there a test header to simulate 429s and webhook firing so I can validate the alert path?
SDK Bot: Use `X-Test-Emulate-429: after=10` to force a 429 after 11th request. For webhook testing use `X-Test-Emulate-Alert: 429_rate=1.5` which triggers the alerts pipeline without actually consuming quota. Don't use emulation for perf numbers.
Hannah Li: Billing rules: will ephemeral keys for perf tests use onboarding credits?
Billing Bot: Ephemeral hosted windows count against onboarding credits. If estimated >$100 include manager approval in the ticket. We also recommend adding `cost_estimate` to the ops ticket to speed review.
Hannah Li: Filed OPS-5402 with keys x2 and cost_estimate $40. CCed Maya.
ops-bot: OPS-5402 created and assigned to Maya Chen.
Maya Chen: Approved OPS-5402. Keys issued, overlap window set to 5 minutes to allow graceful rotation. I enabled a temporary alert webhook to your CI channel for 429_rate > 0.5% over 1m. Keys show up in Console -> API Keys -> Ephemeral.
Hannah Li: Thanks! I'll run sandbox first, then perf and exercise the swap with the emulation header to validate webhooks and backoff. Will revoke keys after.
Ethan Cole: One last tip: instrument your client to log X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After headers; they make diagnosing spikes much easier.
Hannah Li: Will do. Appreciate the help!"
